ei.title: The Subscription Economy: From Ownership to Access
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Jiyun, a high school student, starts her day by logging in to a music streaming service on her smartphone. She enjoys listening to her favorite music, discovering new songs, and exploring new artists every day. For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that provides fresh vegetables and fruits. After school, Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting. For example, she watches various academic lectures to review her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study. During weekends, Jiyun and her family spend quality time together watching movies or dramas using a streaming service. Subscriptions are everywhere To be sure, the subscription economy is a popular economic model nowadays, and Jiyun is actively taking part in it. The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new. Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers. However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more. Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates. Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription. The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers. Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model. From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences. They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts. The rise of the subscription economy is closely connected to two major drivers: changes in consumption trends and the rapid growth of online platforms. People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays. More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things. This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership. For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums. Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers. Moreover, consumers value diversity and customization. The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests. This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes. A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service. It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns. To come to the point, consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions, rather than a uniform purchasing process. Furthermore, consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience. In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost. In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed. This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need. Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience. With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products. If they wish to change their device model, they can do so. Whoever desires an upgrade can get it and experience the latest models. Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers have been able to do numerous things with great ease. In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch. Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices. At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers. By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns. People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn enhances their satisfaction. Services, such as suggesting personalized clothing styles based on customers’ purchase history or recommending videos that match their movie and video viewing history, bring them great satisfaction. Limitations of the subscription economy Although the subscription economy offers many advantages, there are also some disadvantages to consider. One concern is the potential for overconsumption. The convenience and accessibility of the subscription model make it easy for consumers to sign up for multiple services and use a lot of content or products. This can result in excessive consumption and using more subscription services than actually needed. It is crucial to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and avoid subscribing to similar services. Related to the concern of overconsumption is the financial burden that subscriptions can create. While the cost of individual subscriptions may seem affordable, subscribing to multiple services can add up quickly. It is important to carefully consider the costs of these subscriptions to avoid financial strain. Regularly reviewing and canceling unnecessary subscriptions can be beneficial. Additionally, the subscription economy can contribute to environmental pollution. The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment. Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem. Despite the potential limitations of subscription services, they have become deeply embedded in our lives and more and more businesses are jumping onto the subscription economy model. It is expected that new subscription services will be continuously provided to consumers in new areas in the future. We need to have a deeper understanding of the subscription economy and become wise consumers who receive the services that are really needed. Further Reading Happiness Comes From Experiences A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich, a psychology professor at Cornell University, reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t spend your money on things. We assume that the happiness we get from buying something will last as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The trouble with things is that the happiness they provide fades quickly. There are three critical reasons for this. First, we get used to new possessions. What once seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we get used to a new possession, we look for an even better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to compare themselves with others. We buy a new car and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better one, and there’s always someone with a better one. Gilovich and other researchers have found that experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than things. That’s because experiences become a part of our identity. We are not our possessions, but we are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to. “Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really like your material stuff. You can even think that part of your identity is connected to those things, but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On the other hand, your experiences really are part of you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

questions.passage: Jiyun, a high school student, ①<u>starts</u> her day by logging in to a music streaming service on her smartphone.  She enjoys listening to her favorite music, discovering new songs, and ②<u>explore</u> new artists every day.  For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that ③<u>provides</u> fresh vegetables and fruits.  After school, Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting.  For example, she watches various academic lectures to review her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study.  During weekends, Jiyun and her family spend quality time together ④<u>watching</u> movies or dramas using a streaming service.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② explore → exploring: enjoy 뒤에 나란히 이어지는 listening, discovering과 형태를 맞춰야 하므로 -ing형 exploring
det.analysis:
① starts: 'Jiyun ~ starts her day by logging in'은 '지윤이는 로그인하면서 하루를 시작한다'예요. 주어 Jiyun은 한 사람이라 단수예요. 그래서 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙인 starts가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② explore → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'She enjoys listening ~, discovering ~, and exploring new artists'는 '그녀는 듣고, 발견하고, 새 아티스트를 탐색하는 것을 즐긴다'예요. enjoy(즐기다)는 뒤에 -ing(동명사)를 목적어로 써요. 그리고 'A, B, and C'처럼 나란히 이어지는 말은 형태를 똑같이 맞춰야 해요(병렬). 앞의 listening, discovering이 모두 -ing이니 exploring이 되어야 해요. explore(원형)는 형태가 안 맞아 틀려요. ❌ explore는 틀림 ←정답

③ provides: 'a subscription service that provides fresh vegetables'는 '신선한 채소를 제공하는 구독 서비스'예요. 관계대명사 that이 가리키는 주어가 a service(하나의 서비스)라 단수라서 단수 동사 provides가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ watching: 'spend quality time together watching movies'는 '함께 영화를 보며 좋은 시간을 보내다'예요. 'spend + 시간 + -ing'은 '~하면서 시간을 보내다'라는 정해진 표현이라 watching이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: enjoy 뒤 + 병렬(listening, discovering, and ~) → 모두 -ing로 통일: exploring

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① prioritizes → prioritize: 주어 people은 복수라서 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙이지 않고 prioritize
det.analysis:
① prioritizes → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things'는 '점점 더 많은 사람들이 소유보다 경험을 우선시한다'예요. 주어 people(사람들)은 여럿이라 복수예요. 복수 주어일 때는 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙이지 않아요. 그래서 prioritize가 맞고, -s가 붙은 prioritizes는 틀려요. 'More and more'가 앞에 붙어 헷갈리지만 진짜 주어는 people이에요. ❌ prioritizes는 틀림 ←정답

② makes: 'This makes the subscription economy attractive'는 '이것이 구독 경제를 매력적으로 만든다'예요. 주어 This(이것)는 하나라 단수라서 단수 동사 makes가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ subscribing: 'by subscribing to a music streaming service'는 '음악 스트리밍 서비스를 구독함으로써'예요. 전치사 by(~함으로써) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰니 subscribing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ where: 'subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore ~'는 '의류 서비스를 구독하는데, 거기서 소비자들은 ~을 탐색할 수 있다'예요. 앞의 장소·상황(services)을 이어 설명하는 관계부사 where가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 주어가 people(복수)이면 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙이지 않음 → prioritize

questions.passage: Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices ①<u>centered</u> on smartphones, consumers have been able to do numerous things with great ease.  In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or ②<u>purchase</u> the videos they wanted to watch. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ want → wants: whoever(~하는 사람은 누구나)는 단수 취급이라 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙여 wants
det.analysis:
① centered: 'various digital devices centered on smartphones'는 '스마트폰을 중심으로 한 다양한 디지털 기기'예요. 기기가 '중심에 놓인' 것이라 수동의 뜻을 갖는 과거분사 centered가 앞의 명사 devices를 꾸며요. 그래서 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② purchase: 'people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos'는 '사람들은 극장에 가거나 영상을 사는 수밖에 없었다'예요. 'had no choice but to + 동사원형'은 '~하는 수밖에 없었다'라는 표현이에요. 'to go ~ or (to) purchase'처럼 to부정사가 or로 이어지므로 동사원형 purchase가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ want → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'whoever wants to watch a movie can access ~'는 '영화를 보고 싶은 사람은 누구나 ~에 접속할 수 있다'예요. whoever(~하는 사람은 누구나)는 '한 명 한 명'을 뜻해서 단수로 취급해요. 그래서 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙인 wants가 맞고, want는 틀려요. ❌ want는 틀림 ←정답

④ applying: 'By applying AI and big data algorithm technology'는 'AI와 빅데이터 알고리즘 기술을 적용함으로써'예요. 전치사 By(~함으로써) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰니 applying이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: whoever = 단수 취급 → 현재형은 wants (whoever/whatever는 한 명/하나로 봄)

questions.passage: The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new.  Initially it was ①<u>limited</u> to products such as milk and newspapers.  However, these business models have ②<u>disappeared</u> to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more.  Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates.  Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription.  The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.  Companies can have a ③<u>stable</u> revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model.  From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a ④<u>wider</u> range of choices and personalized experiences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② disappeared → expanded: 구독 모델이 모든 산업으로 '확장되었다'는 흐름이라 expanded
det.analysis:
① limited: 'Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers'는 '처음에 그것은 우유와 신문 같은 상품에 국한되어 있었다'예요. 초기에는 몇 가지 품목뿐이었다는 뜻이라 '국한된(limited)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② disappeared → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'these business models have expanded to all industries'로 '이 사업 모델들은 모든 산업으로 확장되었다'예요. 바로 뒤에 오락·기술·패션·교육 등 여러 산업이 나열되니, 모델이 '넓게 퍼졌다(expanded)'는 흐름이에요. disappeared(사라졌다)는 정반대 뜻이라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

③ stable: 'Companies can have a stable revenue'는 '기업은 안정적인 수익을 얻을 수 있다'예요. 구독은 매달 꾸준히 돈이 들어오니 '안정적인(stable)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ wider: 'they can enjoy a wider range of choices'는 '그들은 더 넓은 범위의 선택지를 누릴 수 있다'예요. 소비자에게 이로운 점을 말하는 흐름이라 '더 넓은(wider)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 뒤에 오락·기술·패션·교육 산업이 나열됨 → 모델이 '확장(expanded)'된 것, '사라진(disappeared)' 게 아님

questions.passage: Furthermore, consumers appreciate ①<u>flexibility</u> and convenience.  In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a ②<u>fixed</u> cost.  In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the ③<u>necessary</u> services or products when needed.  This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need.  Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience.  With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products.  If they wish to change their device model, they can do so.  Whoever desires an ④<u>downgrade</u> can get it and experience the latest models.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ downgrade → upgrade: 소비자는 더 좋은 최신 모델로 '업그레이드'하기를 원한다는 흐름이라 upgrade
det.analysis:
① flexibility: 'consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience'는 '소비자들은 유연성과 편리함을 높이 산다'예요. 바로 뒤에 요금을 상황에 맞게 조절하는 예가 나오니 '유연성(flexibility)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② fixed: 'experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost'는 '고정된 비용으로 다양한 제품이나 서비스를 경험한다'예요. 정해진 요금을 내고 여러 가지를 쓴다는 뜻이라 '고정된(fixed)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ necessary: 'choosing only the necessary services or products when needed'는 '필요할 때 필요한 서비스나 제품만 고른다'예요. 꼭 쓸 것만 고른다는 뜻이라 '필요한(necessary)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ downgrade → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'Whoever desires an upgrade can get it and experience the latest models'로 '업그레이드를 원하는 사람은 누구나 그것을 얻어 최신 모델을 경험할 수 있다'예요. 바로 뒤에 '최신 모델(the latest models)'이 나오니 더 좋은 것으로 올리는 '업그레이드(upgrade)'가 맞아요. downgrade(등급을 낮춤)는 정반대 뜻이라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 뒤에 '최신 모델(latest models)' → 더 좋은 것으로 올리는 '업그레이드(upgrade)', '다운그레이드'가 아님

questions.passage: Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers.  However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more.  Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize __________, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates.  Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription.  The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① providing continuing value(지속적인 가치를 제공하는 것): 한 번 팔고 끝나는 상품 대신 계속 이어지는 가치를 준다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize ___'(한 번 팔리고 마는 히트 상품을 만드는 대신, 기업들은 이제 ___ 을 우선시한다). 바로 뒤에 'such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates(새 콘텐츠, 더 많은 개인화, 업데이트 접근)'라는 예가 이어져요. 즉 계속 이어지는 혜택을 준다는 뜻이에요.

✅ ① providing continuing value(지속적인 가치를 제공하는 것): 뒤에 나온 '새 콘텐츠·개인화·업데이트'와 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② selling one-time hit products(한 번 팔리는 히트 상품을 파는 것): 빈칸 앞의 'Instead of(~대신)'가 부정하는 바로 그 방식이라 반대예요.

❌ ③ cutting production expenses(생산 비용을 줄이는 것): 비용 절감 이야기는 나오지 않아요.

❌ ④ removing customer choices(고객의 선택을 없애는 것): 글은 오히려 더 많은 선택과 가치를 준다고 하니 반대예요.
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 예시(새 콘텐츠·개인화·업데이트) = 계속 이어지는 가치 → providing continuing value

questions.passage: People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays.  More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things.  This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without __________.  For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums.  Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② the requirement of ownership(소유의 요건): 소유하지 않고도 서비스를 이용하게 해 준다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without ___'(이것이 구독 경제를 매력적으로 만드는데, 소유 없이도 서비스나 콘텐츠 이용을 제공하기 때문이다). 바로 앞 문장에서 'More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things(점점 더 많은 사람들이 소유보다 경험을 우선시한다)'라고 했어요. 즉 '소유해야 한다는 조건 없이' 쓸 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① the burden of maintenance(관리의 부담): 관리 부담 이야기는 이 문장에 없어요.

✅ ② the requirement of ownership(소유의 요건): 앞 문장 '소유보다 경험'과 이어져 '소유하지 않고도'라는 뜻이라 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ any monthly payment(어떤 월 결제): 구독은 오히려 정기 요금을 내는 것이라 흐름과 안 맞아요.

❌ ④ a stable internet connection(안정적인 인터넷 연결): 인터넷 연결 조건은 언급되지 않아요.
det.tip: 앞 문장 '소유보다 경험 선호' → 소유(ownership)를 요구하지 않는다

questions.passage: Subscriptions are everywhere To be sure, the subscription economy is a popular economic model nowadays, and Jiyun is actively taking part in it.  The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new.  Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers.  However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more.  Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates.  Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription.  The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.  Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model.  From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문 근거: The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 'The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new'로, 구독 사업 모델 개념은 '새롭지 않다'고 했어요. 최근에 처음 나온 새 개념이라는 건 반대예요.

❌ ② 원문은 'Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value'로, 기업은 한 번 팔고 마는 상품 대신 '지속적인 가치'에 집중한다고 했어요. 히트 상품 개발에 집중한다는 건 반대예요.

❌ ③ 원문 'brings advantages for both companies and consumers'는 '기업과 소비자 모두에게 이점을 준다'예요. 소비자에게만 이롭다는 건 대상을 한쪽으로 뒤집은 오답이에요.

✅ ④ 원문 'The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers'(구독 경제는 기업과 소비자 모두에게 이점을 준다)와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: 함정: 개념은 '새롭지 않음' / 이점은 기업·소비자 '양쪽 모두'

ch: 구독 기반 사업 모델은 최근에야 처음 등장한 완전히 새로운 개념이다.
오늘날 기업은 한 번 팔고 끝나는 히트 상품 개발에 집중한다.
구독 경제의 혜택은 소비자에게만 돌아가고 기업에는 없다.
구독 경제는 판매 기업과 이용 소비자 양쪽 모두에게 이점을 준다.

questions.passage: People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays.  More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things.  This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership.  For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums.  Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.  Moreover, consumers value diversity and customization.  The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests.  This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.  A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service.  It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문: 화장품 구독은 각 개인의 피부에 맞춰 '맞춤 제작'하며 '획일적 구매'와 반대라고 함
det.analysis:
❌ ① 이 진술은 본문과 일치해요. 원문 'by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums'(음반을 가질 필요 없이 무한한 음악을 즐긴다)와 맞아요.

❌ ② 이 진술은 본문과 일치해요. 원문 'This aspect ~ is more popular among younger generations'(이런 면은 젊은 세대에게 더 인기가 있다)와 맞아요.

✅ ③ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 원문은 'manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual's unique skin concerns'이고 'a personalized experience ~ rather than a uniform purchasing process'라고 했어요. 즉 개인마다 피부에 맞춰 '맞춤 제작'하고, '획일적인 구매 과정'과는 반대라고 했어요. '모든 고객에게 동일한 제품을 똑같이 제공한다'는 것은 정반대예요. ←정답

❌ ④ 이 진술은 본문과 일치해요. 원문 'consumers value diversity and customization'(소비자들은 다양성과 개인 맞춤화를 중시한다)와 맞아요.
det.tip: 화장품 구독의 핵심 = 개인별 '맞춤 제작'(획일적 제공의 반대)

ch: 음악 스트리밍을 구독하면 음반을 소유하지 않고도 음악을 즐길 수 있다.
구독을 통한 개인 맞춤화 경향은 특히 젊은 세대에게 더 인기가 있다.
화장품 구독 서비스는 모든 고객에게 동일한 제품을 똑같이 제공한다.
소비자들은 다양성과 개인 맞춤화를 중요하게 여긴다.

questions.passage: Furthermore, consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience.  In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost.  In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed.  This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need.  Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience.  With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products. det.korean: ① 원문 근거: In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문 'In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch'(과거에는 극장에 가거나 보고 싶은 영상을 사는 수밖에 없었다)와 일치해요. ←정답

❌ ② 원문은 'these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services'로, 플랫폼이 기업의 맞춤형 상품 제공을 '쉽게' 만든다고 했어요. '어렵게 만든다'는 정반대예요.

❌ ③ 원문은 'In some subscription models ~ for a fixed cost. In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees'로, 고정 요금 모델도 있고 요금을 유연하게 조절하는 모델도 있다고 했어요. '모두 고정 요금제로만' 운영된다는 건 사실이 아니에요.

❌ ④ 원문 'By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers' needs'로, 기업은 AI·빅데이터를 활용해 소비자 요구를 파악한다고 했어요. 데이터를 전혀 안 쓴다는 건 반대예요.
det.tip: 함정: 플랫폼은 맞춤 제공을 '쉽게' 함 / 고정·유연 요금제가 '둘 다' 있음

ch: 과거에는 영화를 보려면 극장에 가거나 영상을 사는 수밖에 없었다.
온라인 플랫폼은 기업이 맞춤형 상품을 제공하기 어렵게 만든다.
모든 구독 모델은 요금을 조정할 수 없는 고정 요금제로만 운영된다.
기업은 소비자 데이터를 전혀 활용하지 않고 상품을 추천한다.

The rise of the subscription economy is closely connected to two major drivers: changes in consumption trends and the rapid growth of online platforms.  People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays.  More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things.  This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership. questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② Owning Less and Accessing More via Subscriptions(구독을 통해 덜 소유하고 더 접근하기)
det.analysis:
글은 구독 경제가 무엇이고, 왜 커지는지(소비 성향 변화·플랫폼 성장), 어떤 장점과 한계가 있는지를 두루 설명해요. 핵심 메시지는 '소유하지 않고도 원하는 서비스를 누린다'는 거예요.

❌ ① Traditional Retail Always Wins Over Subscriptions(전통 소매업이 늘 구독을 이긴다): 글은 오히려 구독 경제의 확산을 말하니 반대예요.

✅ ② Owning Less and Accessing More via Subscriptions(구독을 통해 덜 소유하고 더 접근하기): 소유에서 접근으로 옮겨 가는 글 전체 흐름을 담은 제목이에요. ←정답

❌ ③ Cosmetics as the Sole Subscription Based Industry(구독 기반의 유일한 산업으로서의 화장품): 화장품은 하나의 예일 뿐이고, 구독은 모든 산업으로 확장됐다고 했어요.

❌ ④ The Downfall of Online Platforms Today(오늘날 온라인 플랫폼의 몰락): 플랫폼은 구독 경제를 '이끄는' 힘으로 나오니 정반대예요.
det.tip: 글의 핵심 = 소유(owning)에서 접근(access)으로 → Owning Less, Accessing More

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 filling up their drawers가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers'(의류 구독 서비스를 이용하면, 서랍을 가득 채우지 않고도 다양한 옷 스타일을 경험할 수 있다). 이 글은 '소유하지 않고 경험만 누린다'는 것을 강조해요. 즉 옷을 실제로 사서 서랍에 쌓아 두지 않아도 된다는 뜻이에요.

✅ ① 옷을 실제로 사서 옷장에 쌓아 두는 것: '서랍을 채운다'는 곧 옷을 소유해 쌓아 둔다는 의미라 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ 옷을 자주 세탁해 정리하는 것: 세탁·정리와는 관련이 없어요.

❌ ④ 옷을 친구들에게 나눠 주는 것: 나눔이 아니라 소유·축적을 뜻해요.
det.tip: 구독 = 소유 없이 경험 → 'fill up drawers'는 옷을 사서 쌓아 두는 것(소유)

ch: 옷을 실제로 사서 옷장에 쌓아 두는 것

questions.passage: The rise of the subscription economy is closely connected to two major drivers: changes in consumption trends and the rapid growth of online platforms.  People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays.  More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things.  This makes the subscription economy attractive to <u>them</u> because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership.  For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums.  Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 밑줄 친 them = 앞 문장의 people(경험을 소유보다 중시하는 사람들)
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership.'(이것이 구독 경제를 그들에게 매력적으로 만든다. 소유 없이도 서비스나 콘텐츠에 접근하게 해 주기 때문이다.) 같은 문장 안의 주어는 '구독 경제(the subscription economy)'라서 them이 될 수 없어요. 한 문장 앞을 보면 'More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things'(점점 더 많은 사람들이 소유보다 경험을 우선시한다)가 있어요. 그러니 them은 이 '사람들'을 가리켜요.

✅ ③ 경험을 소유보다 중요하게 여기는 사람들: 앞 문장의 people과 정확히 일치해요. ←정답

❌ ① 구독 서비스를 제공하는 기업들: 기업은 서비스를 제공하는 쪽이지, 구독 경제가 '매력적으로 다가가는' 대상이 아니에요.

❌ ② 음반을 수집하는 애호가들: 오히려 소유하지 않으려는 사람들 이야기라 반대예요.

❌ ④ 온라인 플랫폼을 개발하는 기술자들: 이 문장에는 기술자 이야기가 없어요.
det.tip: 같은 문장 주어(구독 경제)는 them이 될 수 없음 → 앞 문장 people을 가리킴

questions.passage: Limitations of the subscription economy Although the subscription economy offers many advantages, there are also some disadvantages to consider.  One concern is the potential for overconsumption.  The convenience and accessibility of the subscription model make it easy for consumers to sign up for multiple services and use a lot of content or products.  This can result in excessive consumption and using more subscription services than actually needed.  It is crucial to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and __________.  Related to the concern of overconsumption is the financial burden that subscriptions can create.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ avoid subscribing to similar services(비슷한 서비스는 구독하지 않는 것): 과소비를 막으려면 꼭 필요한 것만 구독하라는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'It is crucial to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and ___'(정말 필요한 서비스만 구독하고 ___ 하는 것이 중요하다). 앞에서 구독 모델의 편리함 때문에 여러 서비스를 마구 신청해 '과소비(overconsumption)'로 이어질 수 있다고 경고했어요. 그러니 빈칸에는 과소비를 줄이는 조언이 들어가야 해요.

❌ ① sign up for as many as possible(가능한 한 많이 신청하는 것): 과소비를 부추기는 행동이라 정반대예요.

❌ ② share accounts with other people(다른 사람과 계정을 공유하는 것): 계정 공유 이야기는 나오지 않아요.

✅ ③ avoid subscribing to similar services(비슷한 서비스는 구독을 피하는 것): '필요한 것만 구독하라'는 조언과 이어져 과소비를 막는 방법이라 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ cancel all paid subscriptions(모든 유료 구독을 해지하는 것): 다 끊으라는 게 아니라 필요한 것만 남기라는 것이라 지나쳐요.
det.tip: 과소비 경고 → 꼭 필요한 것만 구독하고 '비슷한 서비스 중복 구독은 피하라'

ch: sign up for as many as possible

questions.passage: The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.  __________ by using the subscription model.  From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences.  They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"기업들은 안정적인 수익을 얻고 고객 충성도를 구축할 수 있다." (10단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, and, build, can, Companies, customer, have, loyalty, revenue, stable 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty
det.analysis:
주어는 '기업들'이라 Companies로 시작해요. '~할 수 있다'는 조동사 can으로 나타내요: Companies can.

조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형을 써요. 이 문장은 '~을 얻고' + '~을 구축할 수 있다' 두 가지가 and로 이어지는 병렬 구조라, 두 동사 모두 원형인 have와 build를 써요: can have ~ and build ~.

무엇을 얻는가 하면 목적어 'a stable revenue(안정적인 수익)'예요: a → stable → revenue.

무엇을 구축하는가 하면 'customer loyalty(고객 충성도)'예요.

순서대로 이으면 Companies / can / have / a / stable / revenue / and / build / customer / loyalty.
det.tip: 조동사 can 뒤 + 병렬(and) → 두 동사 모두 원형: can have ~ and build ~

questions.wa: Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty
accept: Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty

questions.passage: Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices.  At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers.  By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns.  People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn ①<u>enhance</u> their satisfaction.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: enhance → enhances: 관계대명사 which가 앞 문장 내용 전체(단수 취급)를 받으므로 동사에 -s를 붙여 enhances
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn ①<u>enhance</u> their satisfaction.'예요. '사람들은 다양한 선택과 맞춤화를 누리는데, 그것이 결국 그들의 만족을 높여 준다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 콤마 뒤의 which는 앞에 나온 내용 전체('다양한 선택과 맞춤화를 누리는 것')를 받아 '그런데 그것이 ~한다'로 이어 주는 관계대명사예요. 이렇게 앞 내용 전체를 하나로 받을 때는 '하나(단수)'로 취급해요.

주어가 단수이면 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙여야 해요. 그래서 enhance가 아니라 enhances가 되어야 맞아요.

따라서 enhance를 enhances로 고쳐 써요.
det.tip: 콤마+which가 앞 내용 전체를 받으면 단수 취급 → 동사에 -s: enhances

questions.passage: The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests.  This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.  A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service.  It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns.  To come to the point, __________, rather than a uniform purchasing process.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"소비자들은 자신의 개별 피부 상태를 우선시하는 개인 맞춤형 경험을 받는다." (11단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, conditions, consumers, experience, individual, personalized, prioritizes, receive, skin, that, their 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions
det.analysis:
주어는 '소비자들'이라 consumers로 시작하고, 동사 '받는다'는 receive예요: consumers receive.

무엇을 받는가 하면 목적어 'a personalized experience(개인 맞춤형 경험)'예요: a → personalized → experience.

'자신의 개별 피부 상태를 우선시하는'은 앞의 experience를 뒤에서 꾸며 주는 말이에요. 사물(experience)을 꾸밀 때는 관계대명사 that으로 이어요: that prioritizes(우선시하는). experience 하나를 받으니 동사에 -s를 붙여 prioritizes로 써요.

무엇을 우선시하는가 하면 'their individual skin conditions(그들의 개별 피부 상태)'예요: their → individual → skin → conditions.

순서대로 이으면 consumers / receive / a / personalized / experience / that / prioritizes / their / individual / skin / conditions.
det.tip: 사물(experience)을 꾸미는 관계대명사 that / that절 동사는 experience(단수)에 맞춰 prioritizes

questions.wa: consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions
accept: consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions

questions.passage: Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers have been able to do numerous things with great ease.  In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch.  Today, __________ and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices.  At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"영화를 보고 싶은 사람은 누구나 온라인 미디어 구독 플랫폼에 접속할 수 있다."

[ a / access / can / media / movie / online / platforms / subscription / to / watch / wants / whoever ] (12단어) (영어로)

det.korean: whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms
det.analysis:
'~하는 사람은 누구나'는 한 단어로 whoever예요. 이것이 주어 역할을 하며 문장 맨 앞에 와요.

whoever는 '한 명 한 명'을 뜻해 단수로 취급하니, 동사에 -s를 붙여 wants로 써요. '영화를 보고 싶다'는 want 뒤에 to부정사를 붙여 'wants to watch a movie(영화 보기를 원한다)'로 나타내요: wants → to → watch → a → movie.

여기까지가 주어 덩어리('영화를 보고 싶은 사람은 누구나')예요. 이제 '~할 수 있다'는 can access(접속할 수 있다)로 이어요.

무엇에 접속하는가 하면 'online media subscription platforms(온라인 미디어 구독 플랫폼)'예요. 명사를 앞에서 차례로 꾸며 online → media → subscription → platforms 순으로 놓아요.

순서대로 이으면 whoever / wants / to / watch / a / movie / can / access / online / media / subscription / platforms.
det.tip: whoever(단수 취급) wants to watch / 명사 꾸밈 순서: online → media → subscription → platforms

questions.wa: whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms
accept: whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms

questions.passage: In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed.  This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need.  Moreover, __________, enhancing consumers’ convenience.  With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"구독 서비스는 온라인 플랫폼에 의해 쉽게 이용 가능하게 만들어진다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) accessible, are, by, easily, made, online, platforms, services, subscription 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms
det.analysis:
주어는 '구독 서비스'라 subscription services예요.

'~에 의해 만들어진다'라는 수동태이므로 'be동사 + 과거분사(made)' 형태를 써요. 주어가 복수(services)라 be동사는 are를 쓰고, 뒤에 made를 붙여요: are made(만들어진다).

'쉽게 이용 가능하게'는 made 뒤에 이어져 '쉽게(easily) 이용 가능한(accessible)' 상태로 만들어진다는 뜻이에요: easily → accessible.

'~에 의해'는 수동태에서 행위자를 나타내는 by로 이어요: by online platforms(온라인 플랫폼에 의해).

순서대로 이으면 subscription / services / are / made / easily / accessible / by / online / platforms.
det.tip: 수동태 = be(are) + 과거분사(made) / 행위자는 by로: by online platforms

questions.wa: subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms
accept: subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms
